title: Discovery of a Hot Corino in the Bok Globule B335
question: Does the isolated Bok globule protostar B335 (IRAS 19347+0727) harbor a hot corino, i.e. compact emission from saturated complex organic molecules?

what.value: Mass absorption coefficient at 850 um (1.48e-2) and beta index 2.38 for B335, used to get kappa at 1.2 mm (0.0068 cm2/g)

evidence.loc: 4.3 Derivation of Column Density and Fractional Abundance
evidence.quote: which are reported for B335 by (cite: shirley2011)
assuming the systemic velocity of 8.34 km s$^{-1}$ (cite: yen2015)

what.value: Mass-weighted dust temperature 111 K at ~0.5'' beam

evidence.loc: 4.3 Derivation of Column Density and Fractional Abundance
evidence.quote: mass-weighted dust temperature (cite: kauffmann2008) at a roughly 0.5$''$ beam (111 K) reported for B335 by (cite: evans2015)

what.value: COM abundances in IRAS 16293-2422, IRAS 4A, IRAS 2A, L1689B, Orion KL for comparison

evidence.quote: comparable to that reported for the prototypical hot corino IRAS 16293-2422 ($9 \times 10^{-9}$) (cite: jaber2014)

recipe.goal: Image continuum and fit its size/flux
recipe.method: Continuum averaged over line-free channels; Gaussian fit for peak position and deconvolved size

recipe.goal: Identify lines and fit line parameters
recipe.method: Assign lines with CDMS and JPL, assuming v_sys 8.34 km/s; Gaussian fits for intensity, width, v_lsr

recipe.goal: Make moment 0 maps and measure emitting-region sizes
recipe.method: Moment 0 maps of selected lines; deconvolved FWHM sizes for HCOOCH3 and NH2CHO
LTE, optically thin formula using integrated intensity at the continuum peak
assumptions: Tex 100 K as typical of IRAS 16293-2422 COMs and close to 111 K dust temperature

recipe.goal: Derive H2 column density and fractional abundances
recipe.method: H2 column density from peak continuum flux with dust opacity; abundances = N(X)/N(H2)
key_parameters: kappa(1.2 mm)=0.0068 cm2/g; mean molecular weight 2.33
assumptions: Dust temperature equals LTE temperature (100 K)

recipe.goal: Constrain emitting size and protostellar mass
recipe.method: HNCO brightness temperature 4.2 K in beam with Tb<100 K gives diameter >=11 au; line width then gives mass limit (Keplerian or infall)
assumptions: HNCO co-spatial with COMs at 100 K average temperature

evidence.quote: The total integrated flux is 92.8$\pm$2.1 mJy.

answer_key.quantity: Deconvolved size of compact continuum component

evidence.quote: A deconvolved size of the compact component of the continuum emission is 0.43$''$ $\times$ 0.28$''$ with the position angle of 23$\pm$15$^\circ$.

evidence.loc: 4.3 Derivation of Column Density and Fractional Abundance

evidence.quote: In B335, the NH$_2$CHO/HNCO ratio is 0.024
the diameter of the emitting region is estimated to be 11 au or larger
the protostellar mass is estimated to be 0.04 $M_\odot$ or higher, if the motion responsible to the line width is Keplerian.

not_stated_but_needed: CASA version and whether the pipeline or manual calibration was used
CLEAN threshold, masks, cell and image size, number of iterations

Partition functions and spectroscopy entries used for column densities

missing_for_reproduction: CASA version and exact imaging parameters

score_reason: Public data and simple analysis with a clear LTE recipe, but imaging details and software versions are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, numeric abundances from a straightforward LTE recipe, though imaging details must be reconstructed.
